title: The ZTF g/r pulsation amplitude ratio separates hot BLAPs from cool SX Phe stars; a Gaia DR3 and ZTF DR24 search of 2,736 northern stars finds no new BLAP and a new 8.86 min white-dwarf variable
abstract: Question: Can a photometric test that reddening does not change replace a spectrum for the hot/cool decision on blue large-amplitude pulsator (BLAP) candidates, and does a new northern search find new BLAPs? Method: We measured the ratio of the first-harmonic amplitudes in the ZTF DR24 g and r bands (2018-2025). Calibration used 12 catalogued or spectroscopic BLAPs, 138 Gaia DR3 delta Scuti/SX Phe and RR Lyrae control pulsators, and three spectroscopic SX Phe impostors. Then we selected 22,419 blue Gaia DR3 sources (G 13-18.5, Dec > -28 deg) with a large epoch flux scatter, ranked them with ZTF object statistics, and analysed 2,736 ZTF light curves with a multi-harmonic periodogram. Results: BLAPs have A(g)/A(r) = 1.111 (blackbody value at 30 kK: 1.12), and cool pulsators have 1.463 +- 0.049. The class boundary is 1.25. The test classifies all six spectroscopic stars correctly and predicts that the unconfirmed candidate ZGP-BLAP-12 is an SX Phe star. An SDSS A0 spectrum with a halo velocity confirms the cool class of the one ambiguous detection. The search recovers 9 known BLAPs or candidates (9 of 10 analysed known BLAPs at Dec > -20 deg) and several known compact binaries. It finds no new BLAP. Most other 50-75 min detections are SX Phe/HADS stars; four have no catalogue entry. ZTF J193844.94+242931.4, which VSX lists as a delta Scuti star, has a hot ratio and needs a spectrum. The nearby white-dwarf candidate Gaia DR3 2058001302926573568 (155 pc) has a new, coherent, nearly sinusoidal 8.858 min signal with A(g)/A(r) = 1.97. Its cause is probably the rotation of a magnetic or spotted white dwarf. Limitations: The Gaia selection stops at G = 18.5 and loses low-amplitude BLAPs. The reddened low-latitude sample is only 20% complete because of an archive outage, and 3,283 lower-priority stars were not analysed. The classifier has only 12 hot references, and contact binaries also give ratios near 1. No new spectra were taken. Blue triangles: BLAPs; orange squares: spectroscopic SX Phe impostors; gray circles: Gaia delta Scuti and RR Lyrae controls; green diamonds: search detections. Lines: blackbody values at 7.5 and 30 kK and the class boundary (1.25).

Phase-binned ZTF g (blue) and r (orange) light curves. A BLAP has nearly equal g and r amplitudes, an SX Phe star has a larger g amplitude, and the new 8.86 min white-dwarf variable has a g amplitude twice the r amplitude.

Search coverage of the 22,419 Gaia DR3 candidates in Galactic coordinates: analysed, not analysed tier A, other stars with ZTF data, and stars without usable ZTF data. Green diamonds: robust short-period detections.
